page_title: Tintpad | The launcher that falls out of your notch

summary.name: Tintpad
summary.one_liner: A free, open source macOS launcher that uses a hotkey and a notch-style drop panel to open your terminal at a chosen repo with a coding agent (Claude Code or Codex) already running.
use_cases: start a coding agent in a repo with a hotkey
open a fresh worktree branch with an agent running
launch Claude Code or Codex from the menu bar
replace shell aliases for agent sessions
summary.what_it_does: Tintpad is a macOS launcher: you press a hotkey, pick a repo, and press Return, and it opens your terminal at that repo with the agent already running. It drops a black panel from the notch (or below the menu bar on Macs without a notch). It supports Ghostty, iTerm2, kitty, WezTerm, Alacritty, Terminal, and Warp, opening your existing terminal rather than replacing it. Two chips show exactly what Return will run, and skipping permissions is shown in red. Frequently used repos and the last agent and mode used float to the top, and a single keystroke creates a fresh worktree checkout with an agent inside. Claude Code and Codex come preconfigured; other agents with a CLI can be added with one line in Settings.
notable: Notch-style drop panel with hotkey-to-repo-to-Return flow
Supports seven terminals, including Ghostty, iTerm2, kitty, WezTerm, Alacritty, Terminal, and Warp
Frecency ranking of repos and worktree checkout shortcut
MIT licensed, no account, no Pro version, nothing leaves the Mac
caveats: Ghostty requires Accessibility permission to type the command
Terminal and iTerm2 require Automation (AppleScript) permission
Warp has no command API, so the command is placed on the clipboard for the user to paste
